claim: Brown algae utilize phlorotannin as their chemical defense against the predator Aplysia kurodai.
source: Brown algae utilize phlorotannin as their chemical defense against the predator Aplysia kurodai, which uses β-glucosidase (akuBGL) to digest the laminarin in algae into glucose.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known fact about the ecological relationship.

claim: Aplysia kurodai uses β-glucosidase (akuBGL) to digest laminarin in algae into glucose.
source: Brown algae utilize phlorotannin as their chemical defense against the predator Aplysia kurodai, which uses β-glucosidase (akuBGL) to digest the laminarin in algae into glucose.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract describing the digestive mechanism of A. kurodai.

claim: A. kurodai employs Eisenia hydrolysis-enhancing protein (EHEP) as an offense to protect akuBGL activity from phlorotannin inhibition by precipitating phlorotannin.
source: Moreover, A. kurodai employs Eisenia hydrolysis-enhancing protein (EHEP) as an offense to protect akuBGL activity from phlorotannin inhibition by precipitating phlorotannin.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known mechanism.

claim: The structures of apo and tannic acid bound forms of EHEP were determined.
source: To underpin the molecular mechanism of this digestive–defensive–offensive system, we determined the structures of the apo and tannic acid (TNA, a phlorotannin analog) bound forms of EHEP, as well as the apo akuBGL.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract.

claim: The structure of apo akuBGL was determined.
source: To underpin the molecular mechanism of this digestive–defensive–offensive system, we determined the structures of the apo and tannic acid (TNA, a phlorotannin analog) bound forms of EHEP, as well as the apo akuBGL.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract.

claim: EHEP consists of three peritrophin-A domains arranged in a triangular shape.
source: EHEP consisted of three peritrophin-A domains arranged in a triangular shape and bound TNA in the center without significant conformational changes.
evidence: This is a structural finding from the determined EHEP structure.

claim: EHEP binds TNA in the center without significant conformational changes.
source: EHEP consisted of three peritrophin-A domains arranged in a triangular shape and bound TNA in the center without significant conformational changes.
evidence: This is a structural finding from comparing apo and TNA-bound EHEP structures.

claim: EHEP can be resolubilized from phlorotannin precipitation at an alkaline pH.
source: Structural comparison between EHEP and EHEP–TNA led us to find that EHEP can be resolubilized from phlorotannin precipitation at an alkaline pH, which reflects a requirement in the digestive tract.
evidence: This is a finding from structural comparison and experimental validation.

claim: akuBGL contains two GH1 domains, only one of which conserves the active site.
source: akuBGL contained two GH1 domains, only one of which conserved the active site.
evidence: This is a structural finding from the determined akuBGL structure.

claim: Phlorotannin inhibits akuBGL by occupying the substrate-binding pocket.
source: Combining docking analysis, we propose the mechanisms by which phlorotannin inhibits akuBGL by occupying the substrate-binding pocket, and EHEP protects akuBGL against this inhibition by binding with phlorotannin to free the akuBGL pocket.
evidence: This is proposed based on docking analysis results.

claim: EHEP protects akuBGL against phlorotannin inhibition by binding with phlorotannin to free the akuBGL pocket.
source: Combining docking analysis, we propose the mechanisms by which phlorotannin inhibits akuBGL by occupying the substrate-binding pocket, and EHEP protects akuBGL against this inhibition by binding with phlorotannin to free the akuBGL pocket.
evidence: This is proposed based on structural and docking analysis.

claim: Laminarin constitutes 20–30% of brown algae Eisenia bicyclis dry weight.
source: In brown algae Eisenia bicyclis, laminarin is a major storage carbohydrate, constituting 20–30% of algae dry weight.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The sea hare Aplysia kurodai preferentially feeds on E. bicyclis with its 110 and 210 kDa β-glucosidases.
source: The sea hare Aplysia kurodai, a marine gastropod, preferentially feeds on E. bicyclis with its 110 and 210 kDa β-glucosidases (akuBGLs), hydrolyzing the laminarin and releasing large amounts of glucose.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The 110 kDa akuBGL is more sensitive to phlorotannin than the 210 kDa BGL.
source: As the 110 kDa akuBGL is more sensitive to phlorotannin than the 210 kDa BGL (Tsuji et al., 2017), we focused on the 110 kDa akuBGL in this study (hereafter, akuBGL refers to 110 kDa akuBGL).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Incubating E. bicyclis with akuBGL in the presence of EHEP results in increased glucose production because EHEP binds to phlorotannin and forms an insoluble complex.
source: Previous studies have shown that incubating E. bicyclis with akuBGL in the presence of EHEP results in increased glucose production because EHEP binds to phlorotannin and forms an insoluble complex (Tsuji et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The hydrolytic activity of akuBGL decreased with increasing TNA concentration.
source: The inhibition experiments showed that the galactoside hydrolytic activity of akuBGL decreased with increasing TNA concentration, indicating that TNA inhibits akuBGL activity in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: TNA inhibits akuBGL activity in a dose-dependent manner.
source: The inhibition experiments showed that the galactoside hydrolytic activity of akuBGL decreased with increasing TNA concentration, indicating that TNA inhibits akuBGL activity in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Approximately 70% akuBGL activity was inhibited at a TNA concentration of 40 μM.
source: Approximately 70% akuBGL activity was inhibited at a TNA concentration of 40 μM.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the inhibition experiments.

claim: EHEP protects akuBGL activity from TNA inhibition in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Moreover, protection ability analysis revealed that EHEP protects akuBGL activity from TNA inhibition in a dose-dependent manner, as indicated by the recovery of the inhibited akuBGL activity with increasing EHEP concentration (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Approximately 80% of akuBGL activity was recovered at an EHEP concentration of 3.36 μM.
source: Approximately 80% of akuBGL activity was recovered at an EHEP concentration of 3.36 μM.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the protection experiments.

claim: The structure of EHEP was determined using the native-SAD method at a resolution of 1.15 Å.
source: Considering the lack of known homologous proteins of EHEP, we determined the structure of EHEP using the native-SAD method at a resolution of 1.15 Å, with an Rwork and Rfree of 0.18 and 0.19, respectively (Table 1).
evidence: This describes the method and resolution of structure determination.

claim: The residues A21–V227 in purified EHEP were built in the structure.
source: The residues A21–V227 in purified EHEP (1–20 aa were cleaved during maturation) were built, whereas two C-terminal residues were disordered.
evidence: This describes the structural model built from the crystallographic data.

claim: The three PADs of EHEP share a similar structure with an RMSD of 1.065 Å over 46 Cα atoms and only ~20.3% sequence identity.
source: These three PADs share a similar structure, with a root-mean-squared difference (RMSD) of 1.065 Å over 46 Cα atoms and only ~20.3% sequence identity (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: This is a structural comparison result from the determined structure.

claim: The three PADs share a canonical CBM14 fold consisting of two β-sheets containing three N-terminal and two C-terminal antiparallel β-strands.
source: The three PADs share a canonical CBM14 fold consisting of two β-sheets containing three N-terminal and two C-terminal antiparallel β-strands.
evidence: This describes the structural fold observed in the determined structure.

claim: The cleaved N-terminus of Ala21 underwent acetylation.
source: Consistent with the molecular weight results obtained using MALDI–TOF MS (Sun et al., 2020), the apo structure2 (1.4 Å resolution) clearly showed that the cleaved N-terminus of Ala21 underwent acetylation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), demonstrating that EHEP is acetylated in A. kurodai digestive fluid.
evidence: This is supported by structural data and previous MS results.

claim: EHEP is acetylated in A. kurodai digestive fluid.
source: Consistent with the molecular weight results obtained using MALDI–TOF MS (Sun et al., 2020), the apo structure2 (1.4 Å resolution) clearly showed that the cleaved N-terminus of Ala21 underwent acetylation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), demonstrating that EHEP is acetylated in A. kurodai digestive fluid.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observation of acetylation in the purified protein.

claim: RecomEHEP precipitated after incubation with TNA at a comparable level to that of natural EHEP.
source: The results revealed that recomEHEP precipitated after incubation with TNA at a comparable level to that of natural EHEP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), indicating that acetylation is not indispensable for the phlorotannin-binding activity and stabilization of EHEP.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing recomEHEP and natural EHEP.

claim: Acetylation is not indispensable for the phlorotannin-binding activity and stabilization of EHEP.
source: The results revealed that recomEHEP precipitated after incubation with TNA at a comparable level to that of natural EHEP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), indicating that acetylation is not indispensable for the phlorotannin-binding activity and stabilization of EHEP.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparable activity of acetylated and non-acetylated EHEP.

claim: The structure of EHEP complexed with TNA was determined using the soaking method.
source: To understand the mechanism by which TNA binds to EHEP, we determined the structure of EHEP complexed with TNA (EHEP–TNA) using the soaking method.
evidence: This describes the method used to obtain the complex structure.

claim: Both 2Fo–Fc and Fo–Fc maps showed the electron density of 1,2,3,4,6-pentagalloylglucose in the EHEP-TNA structure.
source: In the obtained structure, both 2Fo–Fc and Fo–Fc maps showed the electron density of 1,2,3,4,6-pentagalloylglucose, a core part of TNA missing the five external gallic acids (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the electron density observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The apo EHEP and EHEP–TNA structures are highly similar, with an RMSD value of 0.283 Å for 207 Cα atoms.
source: The apo EHEP and EHEP–TNA structures were highly similar, with an RMSD value of 0.283 Å for 207 Cα atoms (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative structural comparison result.

claim: TNA binds to the center of the triangle formed by the three PADs, a positively charged surface.
source: The EHEP–TNA structure revealed that TNA binds to the center of the triangle formed by the three PADs, a positively charged surface (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the EHEP-TNA complex.

claim: TNA was primarily bound to EHEP via hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions.
source: TNA was primarily bound to EHEP via hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions (Figure 3B).
evidence: This describes the binding interactions observed in the structure.

claim: Resolubilization of the EHEP–phlorotannin precipitate is pH dependent.
source: As hypothesized, resolubilization of the EHEP–phlorotannin precipitate is pH dependent (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The EHEP–TNA precipitate did not resolubilize at pH 7.0.
source: The EHEP–TNA precipitate did not resolubilize at pH 7.0; however, after incubating for >1 hr at pH 7.5, the precipitate started resolubilizing.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from pH-dependent resolubilization experiments.

claim: Most of the EHEP-TNA precipitate rapidly resolubilized at an alkaline pH (≥8.0) after incubation for 15 min.
source: Most of the precipitate rapidly resolubilized at an alkaline pH (≥8.0) after incubation for 15 min.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from pH-dependent resolubilization experiments.

claim: Resolubilized EHEP maintained the native structure and its phlorotannin-precipitate activity.
source: Furthermore, the resolubilized EHEP had the same elution profile as that of the natural EHEP (Figure 3D) in SEC, suggesting that resolubilized EHEP maintained the native structure and its phlorotannin-precipitate activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is inferred from SEC elution profile and activity assay data.

claim: Two akuBGL molecules were observed in an asymmetric unit (MolA and MolB).
source: Two akuBGL molecules were observed in an asymmetric unit (MolA and MolB).
evidence: This describes the crystallographic asymmetric unit content.

claim: The N-terminal 25 residues (M1–D25) of akuBGL were lacking in the structure.
source: These molecules lacked the N-terminal 25 residues (M1–D25), as confirmed by N-terminal sequencing analysis of purified natural akuBGL.
evidence: This is confirmed by N-terminal sequencing data.

claim: The N-terminal fragment of akuBGL was predicted to be a signal peptide using the web server SignalP-5.0.
source: This N-terminal fragment was predicted to be a signal peptide using the web server SignalP-5.0.
evidence: This is a prediction from bioinformatics analysis.

claim: N-glycosylation was observed at three residues: N113, N212, and N645.
source: The electron density map of Fo–Fc revealed N-glycosylation at three residues, that is, N113, N212, and N645 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is observed in the electron density maps of the crystal structure.

claim: MolA and MolB of akuBGL are similar, with an RMSD value of 0.182 for 899 Cα atoms.
source: Except for the difference in visualized glycans resulting from glycosylation, MolA and MolB were similar, with an RMSD value of 0.182 for 899 Cα atoms; therefore, we used MolA for further descriptions and calculations.
evidence: This is a quantitative structural comparison result.

claim: The structure of akuBGL consists of two independent GH1 domains, GH1D1 (L26–T494) and GH1D2 (D513–P978), linked by a long loop (D495–Y512).
source: The structure of akuBGL consisted of two independent GH1 domains, GH1D1 (L26–T494) and GH1D2 (D513–P978), linked by a long loop (D495–Y512) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This describes the overall architecture observed in the structure.

claim: GH1D1 and GH1D2 have a sequence identity of 40.47% and exhibit high structural similarity with an RMSD value of 0.59 Å for 371 Cα atoms.
source: GH1D1 and GH1D2 have a sequence identity of 40.47% and exhibit high structural similarity with an RMSD value of 0.59 Å for 371 Cα atoms (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, upper panel).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of sequence and structure.

claim: In GH1D1, the second glutamate is conserved (E404), but the first glutamate is replaced by D192.
source: Sequence and structure alignment of GH1D1 and GH1D2 of akuBGL with other members of the GH1 family revealed that the second glutamate is conserved (E404), but the first glutamate is replaced by D192 in GH1D1.
evidence: This is observed from sequence and structural alignment.

claim: The oxygen atoms of the side chains between D192 and E404 of GH1D1 are 8.4 Å apart.
source: The oxygen atoms of the side chains between D192 and E404 of GHD1 were 8.4 Å apart.
evidence: This is a distance measurement from the crystal structure.

claim: GH1D2 conserves two glutamic acids (E675 and E885) at the carboxyl termini of β-strands 4 and 7.
source: In contrast, GH1D2 conserved two glutamic acids (E675 and E885) at the carboxyl termini of β-strands 4 and 7; the distance between the oxygen atoms of the E675 and E885 side chains was 5.1 Å (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A bottom panel), similar to that of Neotermes koshunensis BGL (NkBGL, PDB ID 3VIH) (Jeng et al., 2012), Nannochloropsis oceanica BGL (NoBGL, PDB ID 5YJ7) (Dong et al., 2021), and Spodoptera frugiperda BGL (PDB ID 5CG0) (3.9–4.9 Å) (Tamaki et al., 2016).
evidence: This is observed from the crystal structure and compared with other structures.

claim: GH1D1 does not conserve the glycone-binding site (GBS) or catalysis-related residues (CR).
source: Furthermore, regarding the two other conserved essential regions for β-glucosidase activity, namely, the glycone-binding site (GBS) and catalysis-related residues (CR), GH1D1 conserved neither GBS nor CR, whereas GH1D2 conserved both (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is observed from structural and sequence analysis.

claim: GH1D2 conserves both the glycone-binding site (GBS) and catalysis-related residues (CR).
source: Furthermore, regarding the two other conserved essential regions for β-glucosidase activity, namely, the glycone-binding site (GBS) and catalysis-related residues (CR), GH1D1 conserved neither GBS nor CR, whereas GH1D2 conserved both (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is observed from structural and sequence analysis.

claim: GH1D1 does not possess catalytic activity.
source: Altogether, we suggest that GH1D1 does not possess catalytic activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of conserved catalytic residues and proper geometry.

claim: Recombinant GH1D1 did not show any hydrolytic activity toward O-PNG.
source: We expressed and purified the recombinant GH1D1, which did not show any hydrolytic activity toward O-PNG (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E), although we could not rule out the effect of N-glycosylation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental activity assay data.

claim: GH1D2 and NkBGL have broad and crooked pockets.
source: OsBGL and NoBGL have deep, narrow, and straight pockets, whereas GH1D2 and NkBGL have broad and crooked pockets.
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison of active pockets.

claim: OsBGL and NoBGL have deep, narrow, and straight pockets.
source: OsBGL and NoBGL have deep, narrow, and straight pockets, whereas GH1D2 and NkBGL have broad and crooked pockets.
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison of active pockets.

claim: The docking model of akuBGL–TNA showed that seven gallic acid rings of TNA formed an extensive hydrogen bond network with akuBGL in the binding pocket.
source: The docking model of akuBGL–TNA showed that seven gallic acid rings of TNA formed an extensive hydrogen bond network with akuBGL in the binding pocket (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a result from computational docking analysis.

claim: The docking scores of TNA, eckol, and phloroglucinol were −8.8, −7.3, and −5.7 kcal/mol, respectively.
source: The docking scores of the inhibitors TNA, eckol, and phloroglucinol were −8.8, −7.3, and −5.7 kcal/mol, respectively, whereas the substrate laminaritetraose had a docking score of −6.6 kcal/mol.
evidence: These are quantitative results from docking calculations.

claim: The substrate laminaritetraose had a docking score of −6.6 kcal/mol.
source: The docking scores of the inhibitors TNA, eckol, and phloroglucinol were −8.8, −7.3, and −5.7 kcal/mol, respectively, whereas the substrate laminaritetraose had a docking score of −6.6 kcal/mol.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from docking calculations.

claim: The docking scores corroborate well with the inhibition activity toward akuBGL, that TNA had a more robust inhibition activity than phloroglucinol.
source: The docking scores corroborated well with the inhibition activity toward akuBGL, that TNA had a more robust inhibition activity than phloroglucinol (Tsuji et al., 2017), indicating that the docking results are reasonable.
evidence: This is an inference comparing docking scores with known inhibition activities.

claim: The three inhibitors interacted with akuBGL through similar binding mechanisms to occupy the substrate-binding site, suggesting a reversible competitive inhibition mechanism.
source: In summary, the three inhibitors interacted with akuBGL through similar binding mechanisms to occupy the substrate-binding site, suggesting a reversible competitive inhibition mechanism.
evidence: This is inferred from the docking analysis results.

claim: The noncatalytic GH1D1 may act as a chaperone for GH1D2.
source: The noncatalytic GH1D1 may act as a chaperone for GH1D2, as we successfully overexpressed GH1D1 but failed to do the same for GH1D2.
evidence: This is speculated based on differential expression success.

claim: GH1D2 contains an additional auxiliary site composed of aromatic residues in the substrate entrance pocket.
source: GH1D2 contains an additional auxiliary site composed of aromatic residues (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B) in the substrate entrance pocket, which putatively enables it to accommodate a long substrate, contributing to akuBGL activity toward laminarin, as supported by docking calculations (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is observed from structural analysis and supported by docking.

claim: The pH of the digestive fluid of A. kurodai is approximately 5.5.
source: In vivo, the pH of the digestive fluid of A. kurodai is approximately 5.5 (Tsuji et al., 2017), which favors the binding of EHEP to phlorotannin.
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: In the alkaline hindgut, the EHEP–phlorotannin disassociates.
source: In the alkaline hindgut (Lemke et al., 2003), the EHEP–phlorotannin disassociates (Figure 6), and the phlorotannin is subsequently excreted from the anus.
evidence: This is inferred from the pH-dependent binding properties and cited hindgut pH.

claim: The digestive fluid of A. kurodai contains EHEP at a high concentration (>4.4 µM).
source: The digestive fluid of A. kurodai contains EHEP at a high concentration (>4.4 µM) (Tsuji et al., 2017), which is slightly higher than the concentration of EHEP (3.36 µM) that protects akuBGL activity (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: EHEP was predicted to consist of three peritrophin-A domains with a cysteine-spacing pattern of CX15CX5CX9CX12CX5–9C.
source: EHEP was predicted to consist of three peritrophin-A domains (PADs) with a cysteine-spacing pattern of CX15CX5CX9CX12CX5–9C.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from sequence analysis.

claim: TNA has a comparable inhibitory effect on akuBGL to phlorotannin.
source: Previous studies have reported that the phlorotannin-analog TNA has a comparable inhibitory effect on akuBGL to phlorotannin (Tsuji et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: TNA has a pKa of 4.9–8.
source: Meanwhile, TNA has a pKa of 4.9–8 (Lin et al., 2009; Ge et al., 2019; Yi et al., 2011), showing minor negative charges at an acidic pH and the highest negative charge at a pH of >7.0 (Dultz et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature.

claim: EHEP has a positively charged surface at a pH of <6.0.
source: EHEP has a positively charged surface at a pH of <6.0, whereas the surface becomes negatively charged at a pH of >7.0 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is calculated from the structure using electrostatic potential calculations.

claim: EHEP surface becomes negatively charged at a pH of >7.0.
source: EHEP has a positively charged surface at a pH of <6.0, whereas the surface becomes negatively charged at a pH of >7.0 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is calculated from the structure using electrostatic potential calculations.

claim: N-terminal acetylation is associated with various biological functions, such as protein half-life regulation, protein secretion, protein–protein interaction, protein–lipid interaction, metabolism, and apoptosis.
source: N-terminal acetylation is a common modification in eukaryotic proteins. Such acetylation is associated with various biological functions, such as protein half-life regulation, protein secretion, protein–protein interaction, protein–lipid interaction (Silva and Martinho, 2015), metabolism, and apoptosis (Hollebeke et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature as general knowledge.

claim: N-terminal acetylation may stabilize proteins.
source: Furthermore, N-terminal acetylation may stabilize proteins (Lange and Overall, 2011).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature.

claim: The CNo1X15CNo2X5CNo3X9CNo4X12CNo5X5–9CNo6 motif in each PAD of EHEP formed three disulfide bonds between the following pairs: CNo1–CNo3, CNo2–CNo6, and CNo4–CNo5.
source: The CNo1X15CNo2X5CNo3X9CNo4X12CNo5X5–9CNo6 motif (superscripts and subscripts indicate the cysteine number and number of residues between adjacent cysteines, respectively) in each PAD of EHEP formed three disulfide bonds between the following pairs: CNo1–CNo3, CNo2–CNo6, and CNo4–CNo5 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is observed from the crystal structure.

claim: EHEP does not possess chitin-binding activity.
source: In contrast, EHEP and allergen Der p 23 do not possess chitin-binding activity (Tsuji et al., 2017; Mueller et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: Acid catalytic hydrolysis of TNA requires a high temperature of 130°C.
source: Previous studies have shown that acid catalytic hydrolysis of TNA requires a high temperature of 130°C (Jie Fu et al., 2015); even with a polystyrene-hollow sphere catalyst, a temperature of 80°C is required (Luo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature.

claim: The five gallic acids of TNA could not be visualized in the EHEP–TNA structure, most likely due to the structural flexibility of TNA.
source: Therefore, the five gallic acids could not be visualized in the EHEP–TNA structure, most likely due to the structural flexibility of TNA.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of electron density and known properties of TNA.

claim: TNA binding caused a slight increase in the α-helix and β-sheet contents of PAD2 and PAD3.
source: However, the superposition of the two structures showed a decrease in the loop part of EHEP–TNA. TNA binding caused a slight increase in the α-helix and β-sheet contents of PAD2 and PAD3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claim: The binding pocket on the EHEP surface was formed by the C-terminal α-helix of PAD1, the N-terminal α-helix of PAD2, and the middle part (loop) of PAD3 assisted by two long linker loops (LL1 and LL2).
source: The binding pocket on the EHEP surface was formed by the C-terminal α-helix of PAD1, the N-terminal α-helix of PAD2, and the middle part (loop) of PAD3 assisted by two long linker loops (LL1 and LL2).
evidence: This is observed from the EHEP-TNA structure.

claim: Gallic acid1, 4, and 6 interacted with EHEP via hydrogen bonds and additional hydrophobic contacts.
source: Gallic acid1, 4, and 6 interacted with EHEP via hydrogen bonds and additional hydrophobic contacts, whereas gallic acid2 and 3 only interacted hydrophobically with EHEP.
evidence: This is observed from the EHEP-TNA structure.

claim: Gallic acid2 and 3 only interacted hydrophobically with EHEP.
source: Gallic acid1, 4, and 6 interacted with EHEP via hydrogen bonds and additional hydrophobic contacts, whereas gallic acid2 and 3 only interacted hydrophobically with EHEP.
evidence: This is observed from the EHEP-TNA structure.

claim: TNA binds to EHEP without covalent bonds.
source: The EHEP–TNA structure clearly showed that TNA binds to EHEP without covalent bonds, and the binding does not induce significant structural changes; thus, we attempted to recover EHEP from EHEP–TNA precipitates by adjusting the pH.
evidence: This is observed from the EHEP-TNA structure.

claim: The binding of TNA to EHEP does not induce significant structural changes.
source: The EHEP–TNA structure clearly showed that TNA binds to EHEP without covalent bonds, and the binding does not induce significant structural changes; thus, we attempted to recover EHEP from EHEP–TNA precipitates by adjusting the pH.
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison of apo and TNA-bound forms.

claim: All N-glycosylation sites in akuBGL are present on the surface, far from the catalytic site.
source: In akuBGL, all N-glycosylation sites were present on the surface, far from the catalytic site.
evidence: This is observed from the crystal structure.

claim: akuBGL glycosylation does not affect its activity.
source: Therefore, we speculate that akuBGL glycosylation does not affect its activity.
evidence: This is speculated based on the location of glycosylation sites.

claim: There is little interaction between GH1D1 and GH1D2, only in a buried surface area comprising 2% of the total surface (708.9 Å2).
source: There was little interaction between GH1D1 and GH1D2, only in a buried surface area comprising 2% of the total surface (708.9 Å2) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is calculated from the crystal structure.

claim: The distance between the two catalytic oxygen atoms of the side chain of two glutamic acids in GH1 family glucosidases is approximately 5 Å.
source: In general, the distance between the two catalytic oxygen atoms of the side chain of two glutamic acids is approximately 5 Å (Hayashi et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature as general knowledge.

claim: OsBGL and NoBGL hydrolyze laminaribiose with no detectable activity toward laminaritetraose.
source: Such active pocket shapes reflect the substrate preferences of OsBGL and NoBGL; they hydrolyze laminaribiose with no detectable activity toward laminaritetraose (Dong et al., 2021; Opassiri et al., 2003).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature.

claim: NkBGL efficiently hydrolyzes laminaribiose and cellobiose but has weak hydrolytic activity toward laminarin.
source: NkBGL efficiently hydrolyzes laminaribiose and cellobiose but has weak hydrolytic activity toward laminarin (Ni et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from previous literature.

claim: The GH1D2 of akuBGL has similar activity levels toward cellobiose and laminarin.
source: In contrast, the GH1D2 of akuBGL has similar activity levels toward cellobiose and laminarin (Tsuji et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from previous work.

claim: The GH1D2 of akuBGL may recognize larger substrates than that of other BGLs.
source: Therefore, the GH1D2 of akuBGL may recognize larger substrates than that of other BGLs.
evidence: This is inferred from structural features and substrate specificity.

claim: Laminarin typically has a curved conformation.
